quotes.text: Accept Nigerian local payment methods without a local entity.
To request an invite, enter your business email address below.
Payments made with Nigerian payment methods can only be submitted for refund within 365 calendar days

old_evidence.text: Payments made with Nigerian payment methods can only be submitted for refund within 365 calendar days
Stripe accounts in the following countries can accept Naira payments with USD settlement.

findings: New raw lines 5-16 and old raw lines 4-14 retain the Nigeria-local merchant-of-record route: a Nigerian partner is the MoR, no local Nigerian entity is required, and a buyer moves from Stripe's checkout page to the partner/local processor checkout to complete payment. The partner identity must not be collapsed into the separate Stripe Managed Payments product, where Stripe is MoR (wiki/concepts/stripe-managed-payments.md lines 8-21,105-107); source line 35 links that as background only.

Both captures restrict the described customer location to Nigeria, presentment to NGN and business location to US accounts with USD settlement (new raw lines 28-74; old raw lines 27-73). New raw lines 76-85 adds an invite-request path; Dashboard activation at new raw lines 88-103 and source lines 28-30 does not by itself prove an invite, account eligibility or method availability. The curl snippet is a captured example, not an instruction executed in this review.

New raw lines 109-117 now lists Naira card one-time/recurring Yes/Yes, bank transfer Yes/No, wallet No/No. Old raw lines 96-104 listed card Yes/Yes, transfer Yes/Coming soon, wallet Coming soon/No. Current source lines 19-23 and concept lines 20-26 still repeat the old Coming soon values. New overview prose at line 11 nevertheless says a selection of local wallets and cards can be accepted; distinguish this general prose from the specific No/No matrix and leave wallet availability unresolved. Do not infer a launched feature was withdrawn, or that No is permanent.

New raw lines 24-26 and old raw lines 23-25 retain the conditional VAT statement: when the Nigerian MoR provider processes local transactions, it remits customer/buyer VAT, so pricing should include VAT. Source line 26 and concept line 18 omit this conditional scope; keep it alongside the partner-MoR identity and avoid generalizing to all Nigeria sales or Stripe Managed Payments.

New raw lines 38-68 and old raw lines 37-67 retain high-level customer-authenticated confirmation, recurring support at family level, standard payout timing, Connect, no dispute support, manual capture and full/partial refunds. The method table narrows recurring to Naira cards only (new raw lines 113-117); the generic property 'Recurring payments: Yes' is not bank-transfer or wallet support.

New raw lines 101-107 and old raw lines 88-94 retain Payment Intents API navigation and the localized partner redirect. The three-day statement is funds availability in the Stripe account after authorization and approval, while payout timing is separately standard; the redirect or checkout initiation is not payment approval or settlement. Source line 17 compresses redirect, completion and funds availability and should preserve that condition.

New raw lines 119-127 and old raw lines 106-114 retain 365-calendar-day refund submission limit, up-to-seven-day status lag for some transactions (worded from purchase date), and inability to challenge customer/buyer-initiated disputes. Funds leave the Stripe balance when the relevant PSP has accepted a return request and Stripe is notified, not merely when the customer submits a complaint. Source lines 24-25 are mostly accurate but should preserve the acceptance/notification condition.

The primary route is wiki/index.md lines 5-7 to wiki/stripe-index.md lines 421,789 to wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md lines 8-82 and source line 34. Concept lines 25-26 also retain stale Coming soon statuses, so the source and concept need reciprocal dated update. Source frontmatter lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url and only records May provenance; add the trusted URL and November raw while retaining May evidence.

Diff lines 3-64 show textual buyer/customer and VAT link formatting, a changed Elements quickstart link, the invite block, and the two method-table statuses. The refund, dispute, MoR, currency and three-day conditions are retained; link formatting and buyer/customer wording are not separate behavioral changes.
substantive_changes: New invite-request section at new raw lines 76-85, absent between old raw lines 69-75, makes access gating explicit but does not prove any account has been invited or approved.

Method support table changes bank-transfer recurring from Coming soon to No and wallet one-time from Coming soon to No (old raw lines 100-104 versus new raw lines 113-117); Naira card one-time/recurring and bank-transfer one-time remain Yes.

2026-05-08 old raw lines 27-73: NGN/Nigeria, US-account/USD-settlement geography and high-level payment properties.
2026-05-08 old raw lines 75-94: Dashboard/Checkout/Elements/Payment Links and Payment Intents routes, three-day funds-availability condition.
2026-05-08 old raw lines 96-104: bank-transfer recurring and wallet one-time marked Coming soon; retain as historical preview wording, not current availability.
2026-05-08 old raw lines 106-114: 365-day refund submission, possible seven-day status lag and nonchallengeable PSP-accepted disputes.
conflicts: Current source lines 21-22 and concept lines 25-26 say Coming soon for bank-transfer recurring and wallet one-time, while new raw lines 116-117 say No. New raw line 11 still mentions accepting a selection of local wallets; add dated reciprocal qualification and retain this unresolved same-page wallet wording without suggesting withdrawal from live availability.

Current source line 13 and concept line 10 say merchant of record through a Nigerian partner, but their links to Stripe Managed Payments could conflate the legal merchant identity; the separate Managed Payments concept lines 8-10,105-107 says Stripe is MoR. Preserve partner versus Stripe distinction.

Source lines 17,26 and concept lines 17-18 can be read too broadly unless approval precedes three-day funds availability and the partner-VAT statement remains conditional on local MoR processing (new raw lines 24-26,105-107; old raw lines 23-25,92-94).
unresolved_questions: The November invite block does not say whether a previously enabled US Stripe account has access, whether an invitation is sufficient for activation, or when the two table cells changed from Coming soon to No. The same page's wallet-acceptance prose at line 11 and No/No table cell at line 117 do not establish which wallet route, if any, is available.

The overview links method-specific Naira card and bank-transfer integration guides; their bodies were not part of this pinned comparison, so no implementation or runtime outcome is inferred from those links.

source_assessments.reason: The new capture materially changes access presentation and two method availability cells, while the source retains dated Coming soon claims and lacks November provenance/canonical identity. Stable MoR, VAT, funding, refund and dispute facts need their existing qualifications.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/countries/nigeria, new raw lines 5-26 and 28-74 describe Nigerian customers paying in NGN through a Nigerian partner acting as merchant of record, without the business needing a Nigerian entity; the documented merchant geography is US accounts with USD settlement. The buyer leaves Stripe checkout for the partner processor, authorizes and obtains approval before funds become available in the Stripe account after three days (new raw lines 101-107). Cards support one-time and recurring payments; bank transfer supports one-time only; the matrix marks wallet No/No although overview prose mentions local wallets (new raw lines 9-11,109-117). Refunds have a 365-day submission window and PSP-accepted disputes cannot be challenged. Compared with old raw lines 4-25 and 96-114, source-stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md is mostly accurate on the MoR flow but retains old Coming soon cells and omits the new invite request.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/countries/nigeria, the substantive visible changes are the invite-request section (new raw lines 76-85) and bank-transfer recurring and wallet one-time cells changing from Coming soon in old raw lines 100-104 to No in new raw lines 113-117. source-stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md and the Nigeria concept need dated correction; the old preview wording remains historical and No does not establish a prior live withdrawal. The new raw line 11 wallet prose conflicts with its line 117 No/No cell, so wallet availability remains unresolved. Buyer/customer wording, VAT-link formatting and the Elements quickstart link are presentation/navigation changes. The 365-day refund limit, conditional partner VAT remittance, PSP-accepted dispute loss and three-day funds availability after approval remain stable (old raw lines 23-25,92-114; new raw lines 24-26,105-127). The Nigerian partner is MoR here, distinct from Stripe Managed Payments, and neither an invite request nor a browser redirect proves activation, payment success or settlement.
